summary: The facelifted iX is BMW's flagship electric SUV and, since the mid-2025 update, Australia gets exactly one grade: the xDrive45 M Sport at $142,900 before on-road costs. Reviewers are near-unanimous that the bigger 94.8kWh usable pack fixes the old xDrive40's biggest weakness, and that the ride, refinement and cabin quality are a class above the mainstream large EVs, but they split on whether the styling and the screen-led interior justify the money against an Audi Q6 e-tron, Volvo EX90 or Polestar 3. The bigger caveat for buyers is timing and money rather than metal: its 141kWh iX5 successor is due about mid-2027, and early resale values are already well below the sticker, so this is a car to negotiate hard on and hold for a long time.
pros: The 94.8kWh usable pack lifts the claimed range to 602km WLTP best case (522km certified for the Australian car on its standard 21-inch wheels), against just 425km for the xDrive40 it replaced
2500kg braked towing is unusually strong for a large EV SUV and more than double the BMW iX1's 1200kg, with a 500L boot growing to 1750L
22kW three-phase AC charging is rare at any price and lets the big pack refill overnight on a home three-phase supply; DC peaks at 175kW for 10-80% in about 34 minutes
300kW/700Nm dual-motor all-wheel drive for a 5.1-second 0-100km/h, with a smooth ride and hush that Australian reviewers consistently rate above the Tesla Model X and Polestar 3
CarsGuide rates it good value for its class: more standard kit, power and range than the $136,900 xDrive40 Sport it replaced for a $6,000 rise
cons: Australia gets the xDrive45 M Sport only - the longer-range xDrive60 and the M70 are sold overseas but not here - and BMW Australia says the 141kWh iX5 60 xDrive arrives about mid-2027, so today's iX is late in its life
The 602km headline is the best-case end of BMW's own WLTP band; the Australian-spec car is certified at 522km, and EV Database estimates about 470km in real-world mixed driving
Resale is already soft: the carsales price guide values a 2026 car at $121,000-125,800 privately against $142,900 new, and BMW-network demonstrators are advertised well under list
Almost everything routes through the touchscreen, and reviewers single out the missing blind on the panoramic roof, the 2525kg kerb weight and the polarising front end
At $142,900 it clears the Luxury Car Tax and sits far above both the $75,000 and $91,661 FBT exemption thresholds, so a novated lease gets no FBT relief
